sections.label: TCM Research Grant funding
sections.summary: MOH set up a $3 million TCM Research Grant in 2013, awarded $2.6 million to 11 proposals, and added $5 million in 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: In 2013, MOH set up a $3 million TCM Research Grant to encourage collaborative research between researchers in public healthcare institutions, the TCM sector and IHLs, with the objective of better informing effective TCM practices.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: A total of $2.6 million has since been awarded to 11 proposals shortlisted from three grant calls.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: In view of the encouraging response, a further $5 million has been added to the Grant in 2017.

sections.label: CPE points for TCMPs
sections.summary: The target is for all registered TCMPs to accumulate at least 50 CPE points within a two-year period to renew their PCs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The target is for all registered TCMPs to accumulate at least 50 CPE points within a two-year period in order to renew their PCs.

sections.label: Inquiry Committee six-month deadline
sections.summary: The Inquiry Committee has six months from referral of a complaint to complete its inquiry, unless the Board Chairman grants an extension.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The Inquiry Committee will have six months to carry out its inquiry from the date of the referral of a complaint to the Committee, unless the Chairman of the Board grants an extension of time.

sections.label: Interim order stopping practice
sections.summary: New section 26H lets the Board make an interim order requiring a TCMP to immediately stop practice for up to 18 months.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Third, the new section 26H enables the Board to make an interim order that requires a TCMP to immediately stop his practice for a period not exceeding 18 months.

sections.label: Penalties and increased financial penalty
sections.summary: The Board may caution, censure, fine up to $10,000, change conditions, or suspend registration, and clause 7 raises the maximum penalty to $50,000.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Alternatively, the Board may caution or censure the TCMP, impose a financial penalty of up to $10,000, add, delete or replace conditions on his registration for a period not exceeding three years, or suspend his registration for up to three years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: To provide sufficient deterrence and punishment for misconduct so as to protect the safety and interests of the public, clause 7 of the Bill amends section 19 of the Act to increase the maximum financial penalty that can be imposed from $10,000 to $50,000, where the TCMP is found guilty on any ground in section 19(1)(e) to (k) of the Act.

sections.label: Appeals and immediate cancellation
sections.summary: On appeal to the High Court, the Board's decision takes effect only when confirmed, dismissed or withdrawn, subject to new section 19(5A) on immediate cancellation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Where there is an appeal to the High Court, the decision of the Board takes effect only when the High Court confirms the decision or dismisses the appeal, or the appeal is withdrawn.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: However, this is subject to the new section 19(5A), under which the Board's decision to cancel the registration of the TCMP takes immediate effect if the Board certifies that there are grounds to believe that either there is a serious and imminent risk to the public if the cancellation does not take immediate effect, or it is appropriate or requisite that the cancellation takes immediate effect to avoid any actual incident that endangers the public.

sections.label: Warrantless entry and search powers
sections.summary: New section 29 lets appointed investigators enter, search and seize evidence at TCM practice places without a Court warrant.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Under the new section 29, investigators appointed to investigate into offences under the Act or its subsidiary legislation may, without first obtaining a Court warrant, enter and search a place which is used or suspected to be used to carry out any prescribed practice of TCM, or to keep any document, record or thing used in connection with carrying out of the TCM practice, and to seize evidence for the purpose of investigating an offence under the Act.

sections.label: Maximum composition sum
sections.summary: The maximum composition sum is the lower of half the prescribed maximum fine and $2,000.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The maximum composition sum is the lower of one half of the amount of the maximum fine that is prescribed for the offence, and $2,000.

sections.label: Funding for TCMP continual learning
sections.summary: TCMPs can use the TCM Development Grant, capped at $200 yearly, and SkillsFuture funding to defray CPE course costs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: To support TCMPs in their continual learning, TCMPs can tap on the TCM Development Grant, capped at $200 per year, as well as SkillsFuture funding, to defray their costs for attending CPE courses.

sections.label: New generation of TCMPs
sections.summary: More young Singaporeans are choosing TCM as a career, particularly since NTU's 2005 double degree programme.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Indeed, we are seeing a new generation of TCMPs, with more young Singaporeans choosing TCM as a career, particularly since the introduction of the Nanyang Technological University's (NTU's) double degree programme in Biomedical Science and Chinese Medicine in 2005.

sections.label: Concerns over disciplinary process
sections.summary: The speaker is concerned that lacking a formal disciplinary process, penalty schedules and fitness definitions may repeat issues facing the Singapore Medical Council.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Nonetheless, I am concerned that the lack of a more formal disciplinary or inquiry process, and the absence of specific schedules on penalties, and clear definitions of physical and mental fitness for work, may lead to the same issues and criticisms facing disciplinary processes by the Singapore Medical Council today.

sections.label: Investigating overcharging complaints
sections.summary: The speaker asks how Complaints Review Committee complaints about overcharging will be investigated without agreed guidelines, citing five- and six-figure treatment costs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: For other feedback, if there is a complaint to the Complaints Review Committee, for instance, about overcharging, how will such cases be investigated, given that there are no generally agreed guidelines and the spectrum of treatments within TCM is very wide?

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I have heard instances where the cost of TCM treatment could even reach six figures and maybe five figures in many cases.

sections.label: Compulsory CPE and TCMPs
sections.summary: Compulsory CPE is called a step in the right direction, with over 3,000 TCMPs in Singapore and close to 20% inactive.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Second, the introduction of compulsory CPE is certainly a step in the right direction and will help to maintain professional standards.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: There are now over 3,000 TCMPs in Singapore, but I note that close to 20% of them are inactive.

sections.label: TCM Bill, CPE and funding
sections.summary: The Bill strengthens TCM regulation and TCMP standards through mandatory CPE, and the Ministry has provided $8 million since 2013 for collaborative TCM research.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: This would allow for a greater breadth of professional medical opinion on the Board.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It does so through tightening existing disciplinary processes and implementing new mandatory CPE requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Since 2013, the Ministry has provided $8 million in funding for collaborative research projects among researchers and practitioners of TCM and those in our universities and hospitals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As these projects and also research and trials undertaken elsewhere in the world lead to increased adoption of TCM in our healthcare, I hope complementary changes can then also be considered with a view to making the benefits of regulated and professional TCM more easily available to Singaporeans, such as the provision of subsidies for TCM treatment under the Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS) or under the Pioneer Generation Scheme (PG), the increased scope for payment from MediSave funds for TCM items, or the recognition of medical certificates (MCs) issued by TCMPs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   	Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, today's Bill aims to strengthen the regulatory framework for TCM practice in Singapore, and to enhance the professional standards of TCMPs through mandatory CPE requirements, so that local TCMPs and acupuncturists can "keep up with the times".

sections.label: Daily TCM treatment visits
sections.summary: An MOH survey noted about 10,000 Singaporeans visit and seek TCM treatment every day.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: During a recent survey by MOH, it was noted there are about 10,000 Singaporeans who visit and seek TCM treatment every day.

sections.label: Support for compulsory CPE
sections.summary: The speaker firmly supports the compulsory CPE.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Thirdly, pertaining to the compulsory CPE, I firmly support this.

sections.label: TCM Development Grant and CPE points
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Ministry to update on the TCM Development Grant's use and notes the number of CPE points required over two years.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In this context, can the Ministry also update us on the use of the TCM Development Grant?

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Is it just for education or improvement of practice and setup?

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I note also the number of points for CPE required over two years.

sections.label: Maximum fine increase for TCM
sections.summary: The Bill raises the maximum fine from $10,000 to $50,000, which the speaker agrees with in principle but notes is less than the $100,000 under the Medical Registration Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Bill raises the maximum fine from $10,000 to $50,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I agree in principle with the increase, as it strengthens deterrence and punishment in an area where human lives are concerned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, it is unclear to me why this penalty is less than that imposed on Western medical practitioners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Under the Medical Registration Act, medical practitioners face a maximum penalty of $100,000.

sections.label: TCM physician fined for advice
sections.summary: The TCM Practitioners Board fined a physician the maximum $10,000 for recommending a patient delay cancer treatment or surgery.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Last September, the TCM Practitioners Board fined a physician the maximum $10,000 for recommending that a patient delay her cancer treatment or surgery.

sections.label: Communication with former patients
sections.summary: The question asks whether and how the Ministry communicates with former patients when physicians are found guilty of misconduct.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Could the Ministry share whether, and how, it communicates with former patients when physicians are found guilty of misconduct?

sections.label: Disability amended to condition
sections.summary: The section allows cancellation if a practitioner cannot safely or effectively practise TCM due to mental or physical disability, now amended to condition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The section allows the Board to cancel the registration of a practitioner if he "is unable to carry out the prescribed practice of TCM for which he is registered safely or effectively by reason of a mental or physical disability." In this Bill, the phrase "disability" is amended to “condition." I have two questions relating to this point.

sections.label: Defining mental or physical condition
sections.summary: The question asks the Ministry to articulate what constitutes a mental or physical condition or disability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Two, could the Ministry articulate what would constitute a mental or physical condition, or a mental or physical disability?

sections.label: Final adjudicator on judgement
sections.summary: The question asks who is the final adjudicator on this matter of judgement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Who is the final adjudicator on this matter of judgement?

sections.label: Compulsory CPE hours for TCM
sections.summary: Compulsory CPE hours will align TCM professionals with mainstream medical practitioners, and the speaker supports enhanced investigative powers and penalties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The introduction of compulsory CPE hours per year will bring TCM professionals in line with the existing practices for our mainstream medical practitioners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: These will enable them to make better and more accurate diagnosis and care for their patients better.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I certainly support measures to enhance the Ministry's investigative powers and increase the penalties for errant TCMPs.

sections.label: TCM complaint numbers request
sections.summary: An MP asks how many complaints were received each year for the past 10 years and whether the rate fell after TCM registration and certification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Next, I would like to ask the Minister how many complaints have been received so far each year for the past 10 years and whether the rate of such complaints had fallen after the introduction of the registration and certification of TCM.

sections.label: National patient records integration
sections.summary: The question asks whether MOH will look into integrating patient records nationally for assessment and management by mainstream and TCM practitioners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Will MOH also look into the integration of patient records nationally for better assessment and management of patients by both mainstream and TCM medical practitioners?

sections.label: TCM Development Grant uptake
sections.summary: Individual TCMPs can apply for the TCM Development Grant, capped at $200 yearly, and over 400 benefited with claims over $71,000.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: As mentioned in my opening speech, individual TCMPs can already apply for the TCM Development Grant launched last year, capped at $200 per year, to help defray the cost of attending CPE courses.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: I am pleased to share that as at the end of last year, over 400 individual TCMPs have benefited from the Grant, with claims of more than $71,000 made.

sections.label: Compulsory CPE points from 2020
sections.summary: The accumulation of compulsory CPE points will take effect from 2020 after the Bill has been passed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Nonetheless, the accumulation of compulsory CPE points will take effect from 2020 after the Bill has been passed.

sections.label: Higher maximum financial penalty
sections.summary: The maximum financial penalty is proposed to increase from $10,000 to $50,000 to deter and punish misconduct and protect the public.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The proposed increase in maximum financial penalty from $10,000 to $50,000 is to provide sufficient deterrence and punishment for misconduct so as to protect the safety and interests of the public.

sections.label: Board size increased to 11
sections.summary: Taking into account public consultation feedback, the Board size will increase from nine to 11 so more TCMPs can be included.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Taking into account feedback from the public consultation, the size of the Board will be increased from nine to 11 so that more TCMPs can be included on the Board.

sections.label: Bill broadens disability to condition
sections.summary: The amendment Bill changes section 19(1)(k) from "disability" to "condition" to broaden the scope of conditions that may render a TCMP unable to practise TCM safely.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The amendment Bill revises the language in section 19(1)(k) from the term "disability" to "condition" so as to broaden the scope of mental and physical conditions that may render a TCMP unable to practise TCM safely.

sections.label: Registration classes and Tie Da practitioners
sections.summary: There are two registration classes, TCM Physicians and acupuncturists; Tie Da practitioners are not registered under the Act, and Chinese herbal dispensers need not register.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: In response to Prof Fatimah Lateef's request for clarification on the classes of registration, we would like to note that there are currently two classes of registration – practitioners registered as TCM Physicians are able to provide the full range of TCM practice, including acupuncture, while practitioners registered as acupuncturists can only practise acupuncture.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: To Mr Gan Thiam Poh's query on the accreditation of "Tie Da" (跌打) practitioners, "Tie Da" is considered a form of traditional folk medicine passed down from master to apprentice and, hence, Tie Da practitioners are not registered under the Act.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: There is also no requirement for the registration of Chinese herbal dispensers, although herbal dispensers with the relevant qualifications can choose to be listed with the Board.
